I've been doing this rotation for thirty years on this same land in Quzhou. My father did it before me. I know this soil — it's good flat ground on the North China Plain, loamy, decent organic matter if I keep my straw management right.

**My thinking:**

The land all goes wheat in October, then maize right after harvest in June. That's how it's always been. All 13.1 mu rotates through both crops each year.

For **wheat**, I'll use an improved variety — probably Jimai or Shimai, whatever the seed shop in town has that's done well locally the last few years. Not hybrid, wheat doesn't work that way. I put base fertilizer down before I till, then I topdress nitrogen at jointing. I give wheat four waterings: the pre-winter "mengdong shui" is critical for root establishment before the freeze, then jointing, heading, and one more at grain fill if it's dry. I've seen what happens when you skip the winter water — I won't do that. Three spray passes: herbicide in late autumn, fungicide for powdery mildew in spring, and aphid spray before heading.

For **maize**, I've been using Zhengdan 958 or something similar for twenty years. Hybrid seed, no question. I rotary till lightly after wheat harvest, then plant within a week — you want to catch the summer rains early. Maize gets more natural rain than wheat, so I only irrigate twice: once at emergence if it's dry, once around tasseling. One herbicide pass right after emergence, one more spray if I see borer damage. Heavy on the nitrogen at jointing — that's when maize is hungry.

Two people in my household, 13.1 mu, we can manage this ourselves with some hired help at harvest.
